practice.label: How much does it cost?
practice.trap: It's $199 a month — but nothing today, honest!
practice.why: Never quote a number at a door — pricing comes only from Jeff or the founding page, exactly so it never gets misquoted. The approved line names the process, not a price.

practice.label: When do you launch?
practice.trap: We launch next month — get in now!
practice.why: Never invent a date. A made-up launch date is a promise the shop will hold us to. The approved line says what IS happening: roster first, founding spots being claimed.

practice.label: I've tried influencer stuff before.
practice.trap: This one's totally different — I guarantee you'll see results.
practice.weak: Yeah, that stuff's hit or miss.
practice.why: Never promise results, and 'guarantee' is a banned word at the door. The approved line answers with the mechanism: ranked by who lives here, every visit counted.

practice.label: I don't have time for this.
practice.trap: It takes zero time, I swear — just sign here.
practice.weak: OK — I'll come back in a few months then.
practice.why: Don't oversell and don't push a claim. The approved line shrinks the ask honestly: two minutes now, about ten minutes a week later.

practice.label: What if the creator doesn't post?
practice.trap: If they no-show, I'll cover your costs myself.
practice.why: Never invent remedies or spend Jeff's money. The standards ladder in the approved line is the real answer — and founding businesses can see those records.

practice.label: Who else is on this?
practice.trap: Terrapin already signed up — everybody's getting in.
practice.weak: Lots of places — I can't really say which.
practice.why: Never name a shop that hasn't claimed. He may only name shops his own book shows as claimed; otherwise the approved line describes the founding list honestly.

practice.label: I need to think about it / talk to my partner.
practice.trap: If you don't claim today, you'll lose the spot.
practice.weak: OK, I'll check back in a month or so.
practice.why: No pressure closes and no invented scarcity. The card with his code IS the follow-up: it holds the conversation open and credits him if they claim.

practice.label: I'd have to send that to corporate / our group.
practice.trap: Corporate doesn't need to know — it's free to claim.
practice.weak: I can email your corporate office for you.
practice.why: Never route around an owner or a corporate office. Leave the card — the shop carries it up the chain with his code on it.
